subject: Post-call recap: connection reuse & scaling proposal + ratecard
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@globex-analytics.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@globex-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-02 15:12 PDT
Subject: Post-call recap: connection reuse & scaling proposal + ratecard

Hi Alicia / Tom — thanks again for the deep dive today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared record.

Summary of key asks from your side:
- Support long-lived streaming responses (SSE/websocket-style chunking) for inference sessions up to ~60s on average.
- Concurrent active request requirement: target 120 concurrent inference streams during peak windows, with short burst spikes to 200 for <30s.
- Latency target: 95th percentile end-to-end inference < 250ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens).
- Sustained throughput: ~1.2M tokens/day, with traffic concentrated in a 2-3 hour daily window.
- Operational: need audit logs + connection metrics for compliance; prefer region: us-west.

What we proposed on the call (recap):
- Temporary pilot quota to validate streaming concurrency: increase to 120 concurrent streams for 14 days (no code change required on your side; we’ll enable connection reuse + sticky worker routing).
- If pilot looks good, conversion path: Reserved capacity (Dedicated pool) to guarantee baseline throughput and lower unit cost; or monthly commitment to raise hosted quotas.
- Short-term SRE checklist: enable TLS session reuse, set header-based routing to preserve affinity, and instrument the SDK to emit per-connection IDs.

Action items / owners
- Globex: share representative 24h traffic sample (CSV or CloudFront logs) + one example streaming invocation (Tom) — due EOD 2026-09-04.
- Redwood (Monica): enable pilot quota (120 concurrency) and send proposed ratecard and connection-reuse notes — due 2026-09-03.
- Redwood (Ben/Marissa): prepare pricing + impact of reserved capacity vs burst uplift (Ben) and escalate SOC/audit requirements to Solutions (Marissa).

I’ve attached a short proposal and our latest ratecard snapshot (redwood-ratecard-2026.xlsx) so you can see the tiering we discussed. Will enable the pilot once we have the traffic sample.

Thanks — look forward to the logs so we can size the worker pool precisely.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0136
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@globex-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <treynolds@globex-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-02 18:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: connection reuse & scaling proposal + ratecard

Thanks Monica — appreciate the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our infra team:

- The 120 concurrent streams number is per service cluster (we have two clusters behind an NLB). Is the pilot quota per account or per model endpoint? We want to avoid accidental load concentration.
- For streaming: we use persistent HTTP/2 connections with multiplexing today; our sessions tend to open ~3k connections across the cluster during peak. The 60s average is accurate but we also see some long tail sessions up to 5 minutes.
- Token accounting: can you confirm how tokens are billed for streamed partial responses? We need upfront clarity for procurement.

We’ll attach a 24h load snapshot (CloudFront and internal app logs) — will send by the deadline. Also attaching a short doc with our expected SLA requirements for compliance.

Attachments: globex-24h-load-sample.csv, globex-sla-reqs.pdf

Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering — Globex Analytics
agomez@globex-analytics.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-02 19:10 PDT
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: connection reuse & scaling proposal + ratecard

Forwarding Globex reply — key negotiation points below plus proposed approach.

Notes / recommended negotiation posture:
- Clarify pilot scoping: propose pilot quota is per-account but can be scoped to a single endpoint/route for the trial. This reduces cross-cluster surprises.
- Billing clarity: tokens for streamed responses are billed on completed tokens emitted. For partial-in-flight chunks that are retried, we bill completed tokens; keep clear in contract. Ben: confirm language to use in PO.
- Handling long-tail sessions (5m): recommend introducing an idle connection timeout policy for the hosted plan (e.g., 10 minute hard timeout) and a session-priority tier for Dedicated customers.

Pricing proposal (quick sketch for Ben to formalize):
- Hosted pilot: quota bump to 120 concurrent streams for 14 days — free.
- If convert to Reserved Capacity: baseline 50 concurrent streams (guaranteed) + burst pool up to 200 for an additional commit. Pricing: base unit price with 20% discount at $X perM tokens for a 12-month commit (draft in redwood-ratecard-2026.xlsx).
- Alternative: monthly uplift (no commit) to 150 concurrency at 1.3x hosted list rate for predictable months.

Operational asks (Marissa/Markus):
- Prepare short SOC evidence pack for Globex’s compliance doc.
- Engineering: add a note to the pilot to enable TLS session reuse + a connection affinity key so Globex’s cluster mapping remains stable.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Turn on the pilot quota (subject to logs) and email Globex when live.
- Draft the formal pilot terms and shared test plan.

Thoughts? I think the free pilot gives them low friction to test while we lock the language Ben needs for procurement.

— Monica
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@globex-analytics.com>, Tom Reynolds <treynolds@globex-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-09-03 11:30 PDT
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: connection reuse & scaling proposal + ratecard

Alicia / Tom — quick update and confirmed pilot details:

What we enabled
- Pilot quota: 120 concurrent streaming sessions for Globex account (scoped to endpoint /v1/stream/infer) — effective now.
- Logging: we’ve turned on connection-level metrics in the console for your account (connection_id, worker_id, dispatch_latency).

Billing and tokens
- For streamed responses we bill complete tokens emitted. If client retries a chunk, only successfully emitted tokens are billed; we’ll include examples in the pilot terms.

Short-term constraints to watch
- Idle connection hard timeout on hosted plan is 10 minutes. Sessions longer than that will be closed; Dedicated customers can request extended session retention.
- Burst behavior: we allow short spikes to 200 concurrency but sustained above 150 will be throttled; we’ll surface signals in the console.

Next steps / timeline
1) Globex: share the 24h sample + example streaming call (per earlier).
2) Redwood: Ben to send formal price comparison (Hosted uplift vs Dedicated reserve) by 2026-09-06.
3) Check-in: schedule review call 2026-09-16 to review real traffic and decide whether to convert to Reserved Capacity.

Attachments: MAPI_Connection_Reuse_Proposal_v3.pdf, redwood-ratecard-2026.xlsx

If anything urgent pops up while the pilot runs, flag it to me directly and I’ll loop in SRE.

Best — Monica
